sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
Policing on the beat needs many systems, all at once. A emergency call, an SOS or a cyber fraud in its golden hour needs the nearest officer to act straight away — while record searches, cameras, challans, evidence and duty records each come from a different system. SmartCOP brings it together: respond, prevent, record.

The problem

Minutes decide outcomes

An emergency call or a fraud in its golden hour needs the nearest officer moving immediately, not after a phone tree.

Too many separate tools

Record searches, cameras, challans, evidence and duty records each come from a different system with a different login.

Every step must hold up

Evidence, searches and visits must be recorded properly so they stand in court and in audit.

How it works · one emergency call, ring to closed case

  1. CallA citizen dials the emergency number; the control room receives it with location.
  2. DispatchThe nearest unit is identified by distance and ETA, and assigned without a phone call.
  3. RespondThe officer accepts on their phone, navigates, and marks en-route, on-scene and closed.
  4. EvidenceGeotagged, timestamped and hash-registered before upload, sealed in the evidence locker.
  5. ClosedLogged to the response register; the unit returns to available. Every action audit-logged.

Two modules in detail

Facial recognition — a lead, never an identification

The officer points the phone, the platform extracts the biometric template, searches the gallery and returns a ranked candidate.

A match is an investigative lead only. The officer verifies against the record and a supervisor signs off before any action is taken. Every scan, result and sign-off is written to the audit log.

Patrol & beat management

Patrol cars and two-wheelers stream their position continuously. The control room sees who is where, which check-points are covered, and which unit is closest when a call comes in.

Live unit positionsBeat boundaries QR check-pointsCCTV nodes Crime hotspotsNearest-unit dispatch

Built for how police work

  • Biometric login — fingerprint verified and bound to the officer's own device.
  • Every action logged — searches, face scans and each dispatch step recorded for audit.
  • Approval before sensitive data — mobile and tower requests go through two levels of sign-off, tied to a case.
  • A human decides — face matches and AI suggestions are leads; an officer verifies before action.
  • Officer SOS — sends live location to the command centre, alerts the three nearest units and starts body-cam recording.
  • Phone and tablet — the Command Deck adapts: three module columns on a phone, up to five on a tablet.
  • Offline operations — permitted activity continues through network interruptions and reconciles cleanly on reconnect.

sections.title: Safeguards
sections.html:
Safeguards

What it will not do, and what it always keeps.

  • Biometric login, bound to the officer's own device.
  • Every search, face scan and dispatch step recorded for audit.
  • Mobile and tower requests go through two levels of sign-off, tied to a case.
  • Face matches and AI suggestions are leads; an officer verifies before action.
  • Officer SOS sends live location to the command centre, alerts the three nearest units and starts body-cam recording.
  • Offline operations continue through network loss and reconcile on reconnect.
